D: Young Australian light horsemen ride into the famous charge at Beersheba during the First World War.
P: Serve the billy tea when the horses line up for the charge.
S: Chewy oat, coconut and golden syrup biscuits

Golden oat and coconut biscuits made with golden syrup, crisp at the edges and chewy in the centre, the Australian remembrance biscuit. Mix 100g rolled oats, 150g plain flour, 80g desiccated coconut and 120g brown sugar. Melt 125g butter with 2 tbsp golden syrup, then stir in 1 tsp bicarb dissolved in 2 tbsp boiling water so it foams. Pour into the dry mix and stir well. Roll into 16 balls, flatten slightly on lined trays, leaving room to spread, and bake at 170C for 12 to 14 minutes until golden. Cool on the trays to crisp up.
Beersheba camp damper with honey butter
Round damper loaf served warm with honey butter

Crusty camp damper with a soft centre, torn warm and slathered with whipped honey butter and a pinch of sea salt. Rub 60g cold butter into 450g self-raising flour and 1 tsp salt. Stir in 300ml milk to a soft dough and knead briefly. Shape into a round, cut a cross on top and dust with flour. Bake at 200C for 30 minutes until it sounds hollow when tapped. Whip 100g soft butter with 2 tbsp honey and a pinch of sea salt. Serve the damper warm with the honey butter.
M: Light horse camp beef and stout stew
Chuck beef, carrot and onion slow-cooked in stout

Chuck steak slow-braised with stout, onion, carrot and thyme until falling apart, with buttery mash to soak up the gravy. Toss 1kg diced chuck in 2 tbsp flour and brown in batches in oil. Add 2 diced onions, 3 carrots and 2 garlic cloves and cook 5 minutes. Add 2 tbsp tomato paste, 375ml stout, 500ml beef stock, thyme and 2 bay leaves. Cover and simmer gently for 2 hours 30 minutes. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and 100ml milk. Spoon the stew over the mash.
W: Soft dumplings poached in golden syrup sauce

Fluffy dumplings simmered in a buttery golden syrup and brown sugar sauce until sticky, served hot with thick cream. Rub 50g butter into 200g self-raising flour, then stir in 1 egg and 80ml milk to a soft dough. In a wide pan, bring 250ml water, 125ml golden syrup, 80g brown sugar, 30g butter and a squeeze of lemon to the boil. Drop in tablespoons of dough, cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes without lifting the lid. Serve in bowls with the sauce and 200ml thick cream.
K: Strong black tea sweetened with condensed milk

Strong black tea stewed in a billy and sweetened with condensed milk the way the troops drank it, rich and caramel sweet. Bring 1.2L water to the boil in a billy or saucepan. Add 6 black tea bags, take off the heat and steep 5 minutes for a strong brew. Remove the bags. Spoon 1 to 2 tbsp condensed milk into each of 4 enamel mugs, pour over the hot tea and stir until creamy.
